pack.title: Everyday Echoes
pack.description: Kitchens, maps, wardrobes and words with a second life.

categories.title: CITRUS FRUITS
categories.triviaFact: Grapefruit arose in Barbados as a natural cross between the pomelo and the sweet orange.

categories.title: SHADES OF GREEN
categories.triviaFact: Jade is a name shared by two different minerals, jadeite and nephrite, both prized for carving.

categories.title: COFFEE DRINKS
categories.triviaFact: Cappuccino is named after the Capuchin friars, whose brown hooded habits matched the drink's color.

categories.title: ___CAKE
categories.triviaFact: Shortcake is crumbly because short once meant easily broken, describing pastry rich in fat.

redHerrings.note: LIME is also a shade of green, but OLIVE, MINT, EMERALD and JADE already complete the greens, so LIME belongs with the citrus.
CUP suggests coffee, yet the four drinks are complete without it; CUP joins PAN, CHEESE and SHORT to make cakes.

categories.title: BEDDING
categories.triviaFact: The word duvet comes from French, where it originally meant down, the soft feathers used as filling.

categories.title: THINGS WITH KEYS
categories.triviaFact: A map key, also called a legend, explains the symbols and colors used on the map.

categories.title: ___BOARD
categories.triviaFact: Skateboarding and surfing both made their Olympic debuts at the Tokyo 2020 Games, held in 2021.

categories.title: ___CASE
categories.triviaFact: The briefcase is named after briefs, the written case summaries that lawyers carry to court.

redHerrings.note: PILLOW makes pillowcase, but BOOK, SUIT, BRIEF and STAIR already complete the ___CASE set, and the bedding needs PILLOW.
SHEET music sits on a PIANO, but a sheet has no keys; it stays with the bedding.

categories.title: RIVERS
categories.triviaFact: The Danube flows through or along the borders of ten countries, more than any other river.

categories.title: EUROPEAN CAPITALS
categories.triviaFact: Oslo was renamed Christiania in 1624 and only took back its medieval name in 1925.

categories.title: ISLAND NATIONS
categories.triviaFact: The three largest islands of the Maltese archipelago are Malta, Gozo and Comino.

categories.title: FOODS NAMED AFTER PLACES
categories.triviaFact: In Italy, bolognese sauce is called ragù alla bolognese, after the city of Bologna.

redHerrings.note: VIENNA hints at Vienna sausages, but the place-named foods are complete without it, and it is needed as a capital alongside ROME, MADRID and OSLO.
AMAZON may suggest a company or a warrior, but on this board it is simply one of the four great rivers.

categories.title: CREATURES OF THE NIGHT
categories.triviaFact: A hedgehog's back carries thousands of spines, which rise when it curls into a defensive ball.

categories.title: LOUD NOISES
categories.triviaFact: Clatter is an imitative word, meaning its sound echoes the rattling noise it describes.

categories.title: SWUNG TO HIT A BALL
categories.triviaFact: Table tennis rules require black rubber on one side of the paddle and a bright color on the other.

categories.title: HIDDEN NUMBERS
categories.triviaFact: Weight hides eight, and both keep a silent gh that Middle English speakers once pronounced.

redHerrings.note: BAT is a classic night creature, but OWL, BADGER, MOTH and HEDGEHOG fill that group; BAT completes the things swung to hit a ball.
A RACKET is also a loud noise, yet DIN, ROAR, CLATTER and HUBBUB already make four, and the tennis racket is needed.

categories.title: PASTA SHAPES
categories.triviaFact: Farfalle means butterflies in Italian, and the pinched shape is also sold as bow-tie pasta.

categories.title: KITCHEN HERBS
categories.triviaFact: Basil, thyme and mint all belong to the same plant family, known to botanists as Lamiaceae.

categories.title: GIRLS' NAMES FROM PLANTS
categories.triviaFact: Only female holly plants produce the bright red berries that decorate winter wreaths.

categories.title: ___ ROLL
categories.triviaFact: A Swiss roll is a thin sponge cake spread with jam or cream and rolled into a spiral.

redHerrings.note: ROSEMARY is a kitchen herb too, but BASIL, THYME, PARSLEY and DILL complete the herbs, leaving ROSEMARY with the plant-based girls' names.
BASIL is also a first name, but it is traditionally a boy's name, so it cannot join the girls' names.

categories.title: TRADITIONAL TRADES
categories.triviaFact: Plumbers are named after plumbum, the Latin word for lead, once widely used for water pipes.

categories.title: CHESS PIECES
categories.triviaFact: In early chess the bishop was an elephant, a piece Arabic players called al-fil.

categories.title: THINGS WITH A CROWN
categories.triviaFact: Dentists call the part of a tooth visible above the gum line its crown.

categories.title: STARTS WITH A METAL
categories.triviaFact: Irony has nothing to do with iron; it comes from the Greek eironeia, meaning feigned ignorance.

redHerrings.note: KING is a chess piece, but BISHOP, ROOK, PAWN and KNIGHT complete the chess set, and the KING is needed among things with a crown.
PLUMBER secretly hides lead through Latin plumbum, but it does not start with a metal word; it is one of the trades.

categories.title: CLOTHING
categories.triviaFact: In British English a jumper is a knitted sweater, but in American English it is a pinafore dress.

categories.title: DOG SOUNDS
categories.triviaFact: The basenji, an African hunting dog, rarely barks and is known for a yodel-like call.

categories.title: CAR PARTS IN BRITISH ENGLISH
categories.triviaFact: British drivers open the bonnet to check the engine, while American drivers call that panel the hood.

categories.title: HIDDEN BODY PARTS
categories.triviaFact: The shin is the front of the lower leg, where the tibia lies just beneath the skin.

redHerrings.note: BONNET and BOOT are things you wear, but SCARF, GLOVE, JUMPER and SOCK already complete the clothing; here they are British car parts.

categories.title: MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS
categories.triviaFact: Harps appear in Mesopotamian art from more than 4,000 years ago, among the oldest instruments known.

categories.title: BODY ORGANS
categories.triviaFact: The human liver can regrow after part of it is removed, which makes living-donor transplants possible.

categories.title: THINGS YOU CAN BREAK
categories.triviaFact: The phrase broken record comes from scratched vinyl that skips and repeats the same few seconds.

categories.title: ___ BEAN
categories.triviaFact: Coffee beans are really the seeds of a fruit that growers call the coffee cherry.

redHerrings.note: A HEART can be broken, but RECORD, PROMISE, SILENCE and NEWS make four; the body organs need the HEART.
KIDNEY bean is real, but JELLY, BROAD, COFFEE and STRING complete the beans, and KIDNEY is needed among the organs.
ORGAN echoes the body organs, but LIVER, LUNG, HEART and KIDNEY are the organs here; ORGAN is the instrument.
